title_candidates: Give OpenAI Dots a controlled first task
OpenAI Dots arrive with rules, approvals, and pause controls
summary: OpenAI Dots are always-on assistants for eligible paid accounts. A ten-minute first task tests scheduling, rules, activity views, and the pause control.

primary_source.title: Introducing dots
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: Dots are always-on agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that can pursue goals using an isolated cloud computer.
OpenAI says dots can connect to more than 4,000 apps through plugins and can work through their own browser or connected devices.
Users can talk with dots through ChatGPT on desktop, web, and mobile, as well as Slack and Teams; text messaging is planned.
Dots can manage several projects concurrently, report progress, ask questions, and carry context across supported channels.
Proactive background research is read-only: it cannot send messages, change connected-app content, or control a browser or computer.
Users choose which apps a dot can access and can write Custom Rules that allow, require approval for, or block actions; some sensitive actions remain user-only.
Rollout starts with eligible Pro and Business Premium users, while Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare workspaces require an administrator-enabled beta.
One dot is included with Pro or Business Premium, but delegated Codex or ChatGPT Work jobs can still use those products' allowances.

quote_candidates.text: Certain sensitive tasks, such as changing a password, always stay with you.
Dots can still make mistakes, so always review consequential work.

supporting_sources.title: Getting started with your dot
key_facts: Dots are created from ChatGPT on a desktop browser or the desktop app; creation is not currently available on mobile.
The dot profile exposes Custom Rules plus In progress, Scheduled, and Completed activity views.
Users can pause and resume a dot from its profile menu.

supporting_sources.title: Dots privacy, security, and safety FAQs
key_facts: Plugin permissions, Custom Rules, action approvals, and Activity View give users several layers of control, but they do not eliminate mistakes.
Disconnecting a plugin blocks future access but does not erase information the dot already retained.
Deleting the dot removes its conversations, memories, and scheduled tasks, subject to OpenAI's stated retention and legal exceptions.

supporting_sources.title: How we build safety, security, and privacy into dots
key_facts: OpenAI describes isolated cloud workspaces, secure sign-in, prompt-injection defenses, automatic reviews, and confirmation or takeover for consequential actions.

prerequisites: Age 18 or older and Dots access on an eligible Pro, Business Premium, or administrator-enabled workspace account
ChatGPT in a desktop browser or the desktop app

steps.instruction: Open [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com) on desktop, sign in, and select Create your dot. Complete onboarding and give it a name. If the option is absent, your account has not received the gradual rollout; stop and check later.

Open the dot profile, then Customize > Custom rules. Add: ‘Ask me before sending, purchasing, deleting, installing, or changing anything outside this chat.’ Choose Ask before taking action and save it.
Send: ‘Five minutes from now, remind me to review tomorrow’s top priority. Do not use connected apps or contact anyone.’ Confirm the dot says it scheduled the reminder.
Open the dot profile > Scheduled and confirm the reminder and run time. After it runs, check that the update appears in the dot conversation.

Review In progress, Scheduled, and Completed. Then open the profile menu, choose Pause, confirm the Paused label, and resume it. Before using plugins, review Data Controls; remember that disconnecting a plugin stops future access but deleting the dot is what removes its conversations, memories, and schedules.

risk_flags: Dots access is a gradual rollout limited to eligible paid plans and supported markets; the article must not imply universal availability.
Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare access requires an administrator-enabled beta.
The first task uses no plugins or sensitive information and tests the pause control before broader use.
Custom Rules and approvals reduce risk but do not guarantee correct behavior; consequential output and actions require review.
On personal plans, readers should inspect Data Controls before sharing information with a dot.
